_note: Hand-curated. Scope: notable crypto exchanges that have permanently shut down, been seized, or ceased operations, spanning crypto's history. Included for historical reference — links point to reference/news sources, not trading platforms.

items.name: Mt. Gox
items.primaryBusiness: Was once the world's largest bitcoin exchange, handling the majority of global BTC trades
items.closedReason: Collapsed after roughly 850,000 BTC were lost or stolen; filed for bankruptcy in Feb 2014. The largest exchange collapse in crypto history at the time.

items.name: FTX
items.primaryBusiness: Was a major centralized exchange offering spot & derivatives trading
items.closedReason: Collapsed in Nov 2022 after revelations it had misused customer funds; founder Sam Bankman-Fried was later convicted of fraud.

items.name: QuadrigaCX
items.closedReason: Collapsed in 2019 after founder Gerald Cotten died holding sole access to the exchange's cold-storage keys, leaving ~$190M CAD in customer funds inaccessible.

items.name: Cryptopia
items.primaryBusiness: Was a New Zealand-based crypto exchange
items.closedReason: Hacked for an estimated $16M+ in Jan 2019; placed into liquidation later that year.

items.name: BTC-e
items.primaryBusiness: Was one of the earliest major international crypto exchanges
items.closedReason: Seized by US law enforcement in 2017 over alleged money-laundering; operator Alexander Vinnik was later arrested and convicted.

items.name: Bittrex
items.primaryBusiness: Was a major US-founded crypto exchange
items.closedReason: Bittrex's US arm shut down in April 2023 amid SEC action; the international Bittrex Global entity wound down operations in Dec 2024.

items.name: Liquid (QUOINE)
items.primaryBusiness: Was a Japan-founded crypto exchange acquired by FTX in 2022
items.closedReason: Halted withdrawals and collapsed alongside parent company FTX in Nov 2022.

items.name: DMM Bitcoin
items.primaryBusiness: Was a licensed Japanese crypto exchange
items.closedReason: Shut down in Dec 2024 after a ¥48 billion ($305M) hack; remaining customer accounts were transferred to SBI VC Trade.

items.name: LocalBitcoins
items.primaryBusiness: Was a pioneering peer-to-peer bitcoin marketplace
items.closedReason: Shut down in Feb 2023 citing a prolonged bear market and falling trading volumes.

items.name: Paxful
items.primaryBusiness: Was a major peer-to-peer crypto marketplace
items.closedReason: Shut down in Nov 2023 following a co-founder dispute and regulatory pressure.

items.name: Bitfront
items.primaryBusiness: Was a crypto exchange operated by LINE (Naver)
items.closedReason: Wound down in 2023 as parent company LY Corporation exited the exchange business.

items.name: AAX
items.primaryBusiness: Was a Hong Kong/Malta-based crypto exchange
items.closedReason: Froze withdrawals and collapsed in late 2022 after its major shareholder diverted client funds.

items.name: CoinFLEX
items.closedReason: Suspended withdrawals and collapsed in June 2022 after a large counterparty default.

items.name: Voyager Digital
items.primaryBusiness: Was a US crypto brokerage and trading platform
items.closedReason: Filed for bankruptcy in July 2022 after its loans to Three Arrows Capital went unpaid.

items.name: Bitcoin.de
items.primaryBusiness: Was one of Germany's oldest bitcoin marketplaces
items.closedReason: Announced a phased shutdown of retail trading, winding down through 2026.
